findings.title: Payments to Inactive Vendor — Prasad Enterprise (V-046)
findings.description: Four purchase invoices totalling ₹34,50,000 were processed and paid to Prasad Enterprise (V-046) despite the vendor being deactivated on 15-Apr-2025. Payments continued from May 2025 through March 2026.
findings.expected_control: System should block payments to vendors with Inactive status. Vendor master should be reconciled monthly.
findings.observation: SAP Business One did not enforce vendor status check at payment stage. Three invoices were processed by EMP-037 (terminated employee with active access). A bank payment of ₹7,50,000 was made on BT-2025-00011.
findings.root_cause: Lack of automated vendor status validation at invoice processing stage. Terminated employee retained system access enabling unauthorized transactions.
findings.recommendation: Implement hard system block on payments to inactive vendors. Revoke all access for terminated employees immediately. Conduct forensic review of all payments to V-046.

findings.reference: USR-EMP-025, USR-EMP-031, USR-EMP-037, USR-EMP-041, USR-EMP-045, USR-EMP-056, USR-EMP-049
findings.title: 7 Terminated/Resigned Employees with Active System Access
findings.description: Seven employees who have terminated or resigned retain active user accounts across SAP, Tally, Salesforce, and other critical systems. Three of these were terminated over 12 months ago.
findings.expected_control: Access should be revoked within 48 hours of employee separation as per HR-IT SOP. Monthly access review should identify dormant accounts.
findings.observation: EMP-025 (Terminated Sep 2025) has active SAP access. EMP-037 (Terminated Jul 2025) retains Finance Admin access. EMP-045 (Terminated Jun 2025) retains full Admin access. Login activity shows post-termination access on multiple accounts.
findings.root_cause: No automated deprovisioning workflow. Manual process depends on HR notifying IT, which has no SLA or tracking. Monthly access review not being performed.
findings.recommendation: Immediately deactivate all terminated employee accounts. Implement automated deprovisioning triggered by HRMS status change. Establish monthly access certification review.

findings.title: 5 Duplicate Vendor Invoices Detected — Potential Overpayment
findings.description: Analysis identified 5 pairs of invoices from the same vendor with matching amounts submitted within 1-3 days of each other. Total amount at risk: ₹14,50,000.
findings.expected_control: Three-way matching (PO-GRN-Invoice) and duplicate invoice detection before payment processing.
findings.observation: Duplicate check was not automated. Manual verification failed to detect identical amounts from same vendor in consecutive days. Three of the five pairs were fully paid.
findings.root_cause: No automated duplicate invoice detection in SAP. Manual three-way match process lacks systematic comparison of historical invoices.
findings.recommendation: Implement duplicate invoice detection rule (same vendor, same amount, ±5 days). Implement mandatory three-way match. Recover overpayments from vendors.

findings.title: Purchase Order Splitting to Bypass Approval Limits
findings.description: Five consecutive purchase orders to the same vendor were split into amounts between ₹95,000 and ₹99,999 — just below the ₹1,00,000 manager approval threshold. Total value: ₹4,89,475.
findings.expected_control: Aggregate vendor spend should be checked against approval thresholds. System should flag when cumulative POs to same vendor in same month exceed threshold.
findings.observation: All five POs were raised by the same employee within a 3-week period, to the same vendor, for similar items. No consolidation check was performed.
findings.root_cause: No system-level aggregation of PO amounts by vendor/time period. Approval limits checked at individual PO level only.
findings.recommendation: Implement monthly vendor spend aggregation for approval limit enforcement. Train procurement team on anti-splitting policy. Review historical PO patterns for all vendors.

findings.title: Missing Approvals on Purchase Orders Exceeding ₹2,00,000
findings.description: Four purchase orders ranging from ₹2,10,000 to ₹8,50,000 were processed without obtaining the required management approval.
findings.expected_control: POs above ₹2,00,000 require GM/Director approval. System should prevent dispatch without digital approval.
findings.observation: POs were entered directly as 'Approved' without workflow execution. No audit trail of approval/rejection exists in the system.
findings.root_cause: Approval workflow in SAP not enforced. Users can bypass workflow by directly changing PO status.
findings.recommendation: Enforce mandatory workflow approval in SAP. Remove ability to manually override approval status. Implement approval delegation matrix in system.

findings.title: Unauthorized Excessive Discounts on 12 Sales Orders
findings.description: Twelve sales orders carried discounts between 25% and 39%, far exceeding the company policy maximum of 15%. Total discount amount: ₹6,20,000.
findings.expected_control: Discounts above 15% require VP-Sales approval. System should enforce maximum discount ceiling.
findings.observation: Discounts were applied by sales executives without escalation. VP-Sales (EMP-006) did not approve any of the 12 orders. Several discounts of 35-39% applied to single orders.
findings.root_cause: Sales module does not enforce discount ceiling. No approval workflow for above-policy discounts. Manual override possible.
findings.recommendation: Implement hard discount ceiling of 15% in SAP with VP override capability. Retrospectively review all discounts >15% for approval. Recover unauthorized discounts where possible.

findings.title: Employee EMP-035 — Excessive Expense Claims (₹3,69,112 in FY)
findings.description: Employee EMP-035 (Senior Manager-Sales, SALES dept) submitted ₹3,69,112 in expense claims across 12+ transactions, predominantly in 'Client Entertainment' and 'Hotel' categories. Annual expense claim is 4.3x the departmental average.
findings.expected_control: Monthly expense cap of ₹40,000 per employee. Quarterly expense review by department head.
findings.observation: Claims were routinely approved by EMP-017 (GM-Sales) without detailed verification. Several claims lack supporting bills. Claims include weekend dates.
findings.root_cause: No automated expense cap enforcement. Quarterly review not being performed. Approval manager not verifying supporting documents.
findings.recommendation: Implement monthly expense ceiling in Keka HR. Require mandatory receipt upload. Implement random audit of 20% expense claims. Place EMP-035 expenses under enhanced scrutiny.

findings.title: 5 Duplicate Employee Reimbursements Identified
findings.description: Five expense claims appear to be duplicate submissions — same employee, same amount, same description. Total duplicate amount: ₹87,500.
findings.expected_control: System should flag duplicate claims based on employee + amount + date. Unique receipt reference required.
findings.observation: Claims were processed through different submission channels (paper vs. digital). No cross-reference check between paper and digital submissions.
findings.root_cause: Hybrid paper-digital submission process creates opportunity for duplicate claims. No systematic deduplication check.
findings.recommendation: Mandate digital-only expense submissions. Implement duplicate detection based on employee + amount + date window. Recover duplicate payments.

findings.title: Physical Stock Count Discrepancies — 5 Locations
findings.description: Quarterly physical stock count at Q4 FY2026 revealed discrepancies at 5 warehouse locations. Total write-down value: ₹8,30,000.
findings.expected_control: Monthly cycle counts and quarterly full physical count. Variance >2% requires investigation and approval.
findings.observation: WH-02 (Mumbai Hub) showed highest variance at ₹3,20,000. Root causes include quantity mismatch, unrecorded damage, and expired materials. Two adjustments made without QA sign-off.
findings.root_cause: Cycle count frequency insufficient. Warehouse access controls not enforced. Damage reporting not mandatory. Stock adjustments made without proper approval chain.
findings.recommendation: Increase cycle count frequency to monthly. Implement barcode/RFID tracking. Require QA sign-off for all write-offs. Investigate root cause of WH-02 variance specifically.

findings.title: Negative Inventory Occurrences at 4 Locations
findings.description: Four inventory movement records show negative stock levels, indicating issues were recorded before receipts, or stock was issued without system availability check.
findings.expected_control: System should prevent stock issues when available quantity is zero or negative. Goods receipt should precede or be concurrent with issues.
findings.observation: Negative inventory indicates either: (a) physical movement outpaced system recording, (b) unauthorized stock releases, or (c) system bypass of availability check.
findings.root_cause: SAP availability check configured as warning, not block. Warehouse operations ahead of system recording.
findings.recommendation: Configure SAP to hard-block issues below zero stock. Implement same-day GRN posting requirement. Train warehouse staff on system-before-physical protocol.

findings.title: Bank Reconciliation Differences — ₹4,75,000 Unreconciled
findings.description: Nine bank transactions totalling ₹4,75,000 remain unreconciled as of March 2026. These include vendor payments and one payment to inactive vendor V-046.
findings.expected_control: Bank reconciliation within 3 business days of month-end. All items >30 days old should be escalated.
findings.observation: Reconciliation performed manually in Excel. No automated matching. CFO review of reconciliation not documented.
findings.root_cause: Manual bank reconciliation process. No automated matching. Lack of review/approval process.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated bank reconciliation in ERP. Require CFO sign-off on monthly reconciliation. Investigate and clear all items >30 days old.

findings.title: Nine Purchase Invoices Without Supporting Documents
findings.description: Nine purchase invoices totalling ₹12,40,000 were processed without supporting GRN, PO, or delivery documentation.
findings.expected_control: No invoice payment without three-way match documentation. Documents to be attached in DMS before approval.
findings.observation: Invoices were entered directly by EMP-037 (later terminated) and processed through emergency payment channel.
findings.root_cause: Emergency payment channel lacks document requirements. EMP-037 had unrestricted access to process payments.
findings.recommendation: Remove emergency payment bypass capability. Require document upload before invoice approval. Recover missing documentation from vendors.

findings.title: Seven Suspicious Round-Number Purchase Transactions
findings.description: Seven purchase orders carry suspiciously round amounts (₹1,00,000; ₹4,50,000; ₹11,80,000 etc.) which may indicate fabricated or inflated transactions.
findings.expected_control: Purchase amounts should match actual market prices. Variance from standard cost should trigger investigation.
findings.observation: Round amounts are unusual for genuine manufacturing procurement which typically involves calculated weights/quantities. Four of these were processed without supporting market price comparison.
findings.root_cause: No automated variance analysis from standard costs. Manual PO creation allows arbitrary amounts.
findings.recommendation: Implement standard cost master with ±10% tolerance band. Flag any PO amount that is an exact round number for review. Conduct detailed investigation of the 7 identified POs.

findings.title: 8 Sales Orders Just Below ₹5,00,000 Approval Threshold
findings.description: Eight sales orders were priced between ₹4,90,000 and ₹4,99,999 — just below the ₹5,00,000 VP-Sales approval threshold.
findings.expected_control: Cumulative customer order value within 30-day window should be aggregated for approval threshold.
findings.observation: All 8 orders were from different customers but placed within the same month. Individual approvals obtained but aggregate value avoided higher scrutiny.
findings.root_cause: Approval limit checked per transaction rather than per customer per period.
findings.recommendation: Implement rolling 30-day customer value aggregation for approval purposes. Train sales team on anti-splitting policy.

findings.title: 8 Sales Returns Without Credit Notes Issued
findings.description: Eight sales orders marked as 'Returned' have no corresponding credit notes issued, representing potential revenue overstatement of ₹18,60,000.
findings.expected_control: All sales returns must have matching credit notes issued within 7 days. Credit note approval required from Finance.
findings.observation: Returns were recorded in dispatch module but not reflected in accounting. Credit notes were neither initiated nor tracked.
findings.root_cause: No automated workflow between dispatch return and credit note generation. Sales and Finance modules not integrated for returns.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated credit note generation upon return receipt. Reconcile dispatch returns with accounting monthly. Issue pending credit notes immediately.

findings.title: Ghost Employee — Salary Paid to Non-Existent Employee
findings.description: A salary payment of ₹42,300 was made in January 2026 to 'EMP-105' (Phantom Employee) with bank account HDFC-9988776655. This employee ID does not exist in the HRMS.
findings.expected_control: Monthly payroll reconciliation between HRMS, payroll system, and bank payments. New employee additions require HR approval.
findings.observation: Payroll entry was added manually to the payroll file without HRMS validation. Bank payment was processed without verification against approved employee list.
findings.root_cause: Payroll processing does not validate employee IDs against HRMS master. Manual entries possible in payroll file.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated HRMS-to-payroll validation. Require dual authorization for manual payroll additions. Investigate origin of EMP-105 entry. Recover ₹42,300.

findings.title: Segregation of Duties Violation — IT Admin with Finance Access
findings.description: EMP-004 (Head-IT) holds Finance Admin role in SAP Business One, violating the principle that IT administrators should not have transactional access to financial modules.
findings.expected_control: IT admin role should be limited to system administration. Finance module access requires separate authorization with CFO approval.
findings.observation: EMP-004 has both IT Admin and Finance Admin roles, enabling creation/modification of financial master data and transactions without independent oversight.
findings.root_cause: Role assignment done during initial implementation without SoD review. No periodic access review.
findings.recommendation: Remove Finance Admin role from IT personnel. Implement role-based access control with SoD matrix. Conduct quarterly access reviews.

findings.title: Month-End Revenue Recognition Irregularities
findings.description: Unusual concentration of high-value sales orders (₹20-50L each) on the last 3 days of June, September, and December 2025. Total month-end revenue: ₹2,20,00,000.
findings.expected_control: Revenue recognition per Ind AS 115 — control transfers on delivery. Month-end cut-off procedures.
findings.observation: Several orders dated month-end were dispatched in the following month, suggesting premature revenue recognition. Order values are 3-5x the monthly average for those customers.
findings.root_cause: Revenue recognition not strictly tied to delivery proof. Pressure to meet quarterly targets.
findings.recommendation: Enforce revenue recognition only upon delivery confirmation. Review all month-end transactions for proper cut-off. Implement independent Finance review of last-3-day transactions.

findings.title: Late/Overdue Tax Payments — ₹15,50,000
findings.description: Four tax payments (GST and TDS) were either paid late or remain overdue. Late payments attract interest and penalties under respective acts.
findings.expected_control: Tax payments processed at least 5 days before due date. Automated reminders for upcoming tax deadlines.
findings.observation: GST payment for June 2025 was made on due date itself (late as per GST Act). TDS payments for Sep and Dec 2025 are still outstanding.
findings.root_cause: Manual tax payment process. No automated calendar/reminders. Finance team understaffed during peak periods.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated tax payment calendar with reminders. Process tax payments T-5 minimum. Set up penalty budget for historical late payments.

findings.title: 4 Purchase Invoices Without PO Reference — Procurement Bypass
findings.description: Four purchase invoices totaling ₹12,80,000 were processed without any PO reference, bypassing the entire procurement workflow.
findings.expected_control: All purchases above ₹10,000 require a purchase order. Invoice without PO requires CFO exception approval.
findings.observation: Invoices entered as direct purchases. No exception approval documentation found.
findings.root_cause: Direct purchase capability not restricted in ERP. No monitoring of PO-less invoices.
findings.recommendation: Block direct invoice entry above ₹10,000 in SAP. Monitor PO-less invoices monthly. Require CFO approval for any exception.

findings.title: 8 Invoices with Failed Three-Way Match
findings.description: Eight purchase invoices failed three-way matching — either PO amount, GRN quantity, or invoice amount did not match within tolerance.
findings.expected_control: Three-way match required with ±2% tolerance before payment processing.
findings.observation: Invoices were force-posted by finance team to meet vendor payment deadlines, overriding match exception.
findings.root_cause: Three-way match exceptions override not controlled. Time pressure from vendor payment terms.
findings.recommendation: Implement mandatory authorization for three-way match exceptions. Limit override to CFO level. Track exception frequency by processor.

findings.title: 3 Backdated Purchase Order Approvals
findings.description: Three purchase orders show approval dates earlier than the PO creation date, indicating backdating of approval records.
findings.expected_control: PO approval date must be on or after PO creation date. System timestamp to be immutable.
findings.observation: Audit trail shows approval timestamp preceding PO creation timestamp by 5-15 days for three POs.
findings.root_cause: SAP workflow allows manual date entry for approvals. Audit trail timestamps can be modified by admin users.
findings.recommendation: Enforce system-generated timestamps for all workflow steps. Restrict date modification capability. Implement audit trail integrity checks.

findings.title: 52 Off-Hours System Access Activities Detected
findings.description: 52 login sessions occurred outside business hours (before 8 AM or after 7 PM), including some on weekends and holidays.
findings.expected_control: Off-hours access should require VPN + MFA + manager pre-approval. Unusual access patterns should trigger alerts.
findings.observation: No off-hours access policy exists. MFA is not enforced for 19 users. Some off-hours logins from terminated employee accounts.
findings.root_cause: No off-hours access policy. MFA not universally enforced. No anomaly detection in place.
findings.recommendation: Implement off-hours access policy requiring pre-approval. Enforce MFA for all users. Implement real-time anomaly detection for access patterns.

findings.title: 58 Expense Claims Without Supporting Documentation
findings.description: 58 expense claims totalling approximately ₹4,50,000 were submitted and approved without attaching supporting bills or receipts.
findings.expected_control: Mandatory document upload for all expense claims above ₹1,000. Random audit of 20% claims.
findings.observation: Claims marked as 'None' for supporting docs were still approved and paid. No verification performed by approvers.
findings.root_cause: Expense system allows submission without mandatory document upload. Approvers not verifying documentation.
findings.recommendation: Make document upload mandatory in expense system. Implement random audit program. Recover claims without documentation.

findings.title: 3 Vendor Payments Made Outside Business Hours
findings.description: Three large vendor payments (₹5,00,000 to ₹20,00,000) were executed between 10 PM and 2 AM, which is unusual for corporate banking.
findings.expected_control: All bank payments above ₹2,00,000 require dual authorization during business hours. Off-hours payments flagged for next-day review.
findings.observation: Payments were processed through CorpConnect with single authorization. No off-hours payment policy exists.
findings.root_cause: HDFC CorpConnect allows 24x7 payments without time-based restrictions. No dual authorization for high-value payments.
findings.recommendation: Implement time-based payment restrictions on CorpConnect. Require dual authorization for payments >₹2L. Flag all off-hours transactions for CFO review.

findings.title: 19 Users Without Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
findings.description: 19 user accounts (37% of sampled users) do not have MFA enabled, including users with admin-level access to SAP and financial systems.
findings.expected_control: MFA mandatory for all users accessing ERP, financial, and banking systems.
findings.observation: MFA was configured as optional during implementation. IT has not enforced MFA policy.
findings.root_cause: MFA deployment incomplete. No policy mandate from management.
findings.recommendation: Enforce MFA for all users within 30 days. Prioritize admin and finance users. Block non-MFA access after grace period.

findings.title: Payment to Dormant Vendor — Shree Trading Co (V-047)
findings.description: A purchase order of ₹5,31,000 and subsequent payment was made to Shree Trading Co (V-047), which had been classified as Dormant since March 2025 with no transactions for 12+ months.
findings.expected_control: Dormant vendors should require reactivation approval before any new transactions. System should block new POs to dormant vendors.
findings.observation: Vendor was reactivated without proper due diligence. No reactivation approval found. Payment processed normally.
findings.root_cause: Dormant vendor status not enforced in procurement workflow. Reactivation process informal.
findings.recommendation: Implement formal vendor reactivation workflow with due diligence requirements. Block dormant vendors in system. Review all transactions with dormant vendors in FY26.

findings.title: Privilege Creep — Multiple Users with Excessive Access Rights
findings.description: Access review revealed 8 users with system privileges exceeding their role requirements. Includes warehouse operators with purchase module access and sales staff with inventory adjustment rights.
findings.expected_control: Role-based access control (RBAC) with least privilege principle. Quarterly access review.
findings.observation: Initial SAP implementation gave broad access to minimize support tickets. Access never reviewed or reduced.
findings.root_cause: Access granted during go-live without RBAC design. No periodic access certification.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC with role definitions. Remove excess privileges. Establish quarterly access certification process.

findings.title: Damaged Inventory Written Off Without Approval
findings.description: Three damaged inventory write-off entries (total ₹1,65,000) were processed without Quality Assurance sign-off and Plant Head approval.
findings.expected_control: Inventory write-off requires QA inspection report, Plant Head approval, and CFO sign-off above ₹50,000.
findings.observation: Warehouse staff processed write-offs directly in SAP. No quality inspection performed. No management approval documented.
findings.root_cause: Write-off workflow not enforced in SAP. Warehouse staff have direct inventory adjustment access.
findings.recommendation: Implement multi-level approval workflow for inventory adjustments. Restrict inventory adjustment access. Require QA inspection for all write-offs.

findings.title: 4 Segregation of Duties Violations Identified
findings.description: Four SoD violations found: (1) Self-approved purchase orders, (2) Sales person approving own discounts, (3) Warehouse keeper approving write-offs, (4) IT admin with finance access.
findings.expected_control: Segregation of duties matrix enforced through system access controls. Dual authorization for critical transactions.
findings.observation: SoD matrix defined in policy but not enforced in SAP. Role assignments allow same person to perform conflicting duties.
findings.root_cause: SAP role design did not incorporate SoD rules. No SoD monitoring tool in place.
findings.recommendation: Implement SoD rules in SAP GRC. Map all critical transactions to SoD matrix. Remediate all identified violations within 60 days.

findings.title: GST Payment Amount Variance — ₹1,50,000
findings.description: GST payment for August 2025 shows ₹1,50,000 variance between the amount declared in GSTR-3B return and the actual payment made.
findings.expected_control: Tax payment amount must match GSTR-3B/TDS return amounts. Monthly reconciliation required.
findings.observation: Payment was ₹1,50,000 higher than the declared amount. Possible overpayment or misclassification.
findings.root_cause: Manual data entry error in bank payment. No reconciliation between return and payment.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated reconciliation between tax returns and payments. File for refund of overpayment.

findings.title: Suspicious Round-Number Purchase Invoices — 9 Instances
findings.description: Nine purchase invoices carry exact round-number amounts (multiples of ₹1,000 or ₹10,000), which is atypical for genuine manufacturing procurement.
findings.expected_control: Invoice amounts should reflect actual goods/services with specific quantities and rates.
findings.observation: Genuine manufacturing invoices typically result in non-round amounts due to weight-based pricing, GST calculations, etc. Round amounts may indicate fabrication.
findings.root_cause: No automated validation of invoice amounts against standard pricing. Manual entry allows arbitrary amounts.
findings.recommendation: Flag round-number invoices for mandatory review. Cross-reference invoice amounts with contract rates and market prices.

findings.title: 6 Weekend/Holiday Expense Claims
findings.description: Six expense claims show expense dates falling on weekends, suggesting either fraudulent claims or poor record-keeping.
findings.expected_control: Expense dates should match actual business travel/activity dates. Weekend claims require special justification.
findings.observation: Claims include hotel stays and travel expenses on Saturdays/Sundays with no weekend travel authorization.
findings.root_cause: No validation of expense dates against working calendar. Weekend travel not requiring pre-approval.
findings.recommendation: Implement calendar-based expense date validation. Require pre-approval for weekend travel.

findings.title: 8 Expense Claims Exceeding Per-Diem Limits
findings.description: Eight client entertainment expense claims ranging from ₹35,000 to ₹65,000 significantly exceed the per-diem limit of ₹5,000 per event.
findings.expected_control: Per-diem limits enforced for each expense category. Exceeding amounts require VP-level approval.
findings.observation: Claims approved at department manager level without escalation. No per-diem compliance check in expense system.
findings.root_cause: Per-diem limits not configured in expense system. Manual approval without limit check.
findings.recommendation: Configure per-diem limits in Keka HR. Auto-escalate claims exceeding limits. Train approvers on policy compliance.

findings.title: Sales to Customers with Overdue Balances — Credit Policy Violation
findings.description: Five sales orders were dispatched to customers who already had overdue payments exceeding their credit terms.
findings.expected_control: System should block dispatch to customers with overdue invoices past credit terms. Credit limit enforcement.
findings.observation: Credit check not configured in SAP dispatch module. Sales team manually overrode credit blocks.
findings.root_cause: Credit management not integrated with dispatch module. Manual credit block overrides not tracked.
findings.recommendation: Integrate credit management with dispatch. Implement automatic credit hold for overdue accounts. Track and require justification for all credit overrides.

findings.title: 7 Departments Significantly Over Budget
findings.description: Seven departments exceeded their annual budgets by 5-27%. R&D exceeded by 27.3%, IT by 22.2%, and Sales by 20.0%. Total over-budget amount: ₹2,12,00,000.
findings.expected_control: Quarterly budget reviews with variance analysis. Expenditure controls for amounts exceeding quarterly allocation.
findings.observation: Budget overruns not flagged during the year. No mid-year budget revision process. IT overrun due to unplanned infrastructure purchase not approved by CFO.
findings.root_cause: Budget monitoring done annually, not quarterly. No automated alerts for budget threshold breaches.
findings.recommendation: Implement quarterly budget review process. Set up automated alerts at 80% and 100% of budget. Require CFO approval for expenditure above quarterly allocation.

findings.title: Invoices by Terminated Employee — Unauthorized Processing
findings.description: Three purchase invoices were processed by EMP-037 after their termination date of July 1, 2025. The employee retained Finance Admin access in Tally.
findings.expected_control: User access revoked within 24 hours of termination. Tally access reviewed monthly.
findings.observation: EMP-037's Tally login was used to process invoices in Aug, Sep, and Oct 2025 — months after termination.
findings.root_cause: Tally access not linked to HRMS termination status. No automated deprovisioning for accounting system.
findings.recommendation: Immediately revoke EMP-037's Tally access. Investigate all transactions processed post-termination. Implement HRMS-ERP access linkage.

findings.title: 7 Ex-Employees Without Exit Clearance Documentation
findings.description: Seven employees who left the organization did not complete the formal exit clearance process, including IT asset return, ID card return, and no-dues certification.
findings.expected_control: Exit clearance checklist completed within 24 hours of last working day. System access revoked only after clearance.
findings.observation: Exit process relies on manual forms. No tracking in HRMS. IT assets not recovered from 3 employees.
findings.root_cause: Manual exit process with no tracking. No integration between HRMS and IT deprovisioning.
findings.recommendation: Implement digital exit clearance checklist in HRMS. Track IT asset return. Make exit clearance mandatory before final settlement.

findings.reference: Multiple POs to V-045, V-046, V-047
findings.title: Low-Rated Vendor Concentration — Vendor Due Diligence Gaps
findings.description: Three vendors with ratings below 3.0 (V-045: 3.2, V-046: 2.8, V-047: 2.5) received total payments of ₹83,00,000 during FY26 despite poor performance ratings.
findings.expected_control: Vendors rated below 3.0 should be on probation with enhanced scrutiny. Spending capped until rating improves.
findings.observation: No vendor probation mechanism exists. Low-rated vendors continue to receive full order volumes.
findings.root_cause: Vendor rating system exists but has no operational impact. No probation/quarantine process.
findings.recommendation: Implement vendor probation mechanism with spending limits. Require enhanced approval for low-rated vendors. Review due diligence for V-045, V-046, V-047 specifically.

findings.title: 5 Suspicious Round-Number Bank Payments
findings.description: Five bank debit transactions carry exact round amounts (₹1,00,000 to ₹7,50,000), which is atypical for manufacturing vendor payments.
findings.expected_control: Bank payments should match invoice amounts. Round-number payments flagged for review.
findings.observation: Genuine vendor payments based on invoice amounts rarely result in exact round numbers. These payments may indicate fictitious transactions or diversion of funds.
findings.root_cause: No validation of bank payment amounts against underlying invoices. Manual payment processing.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated validation: bank payment amount must match invoice within ±1%. Flag all round-number payments for mandatory review.
